correctness.rationale: Under the exact DCT-II normalization of Kim et al. 2023, twice differentiating the finite cosine Dirichlet kernel at integer multiples of pi/N gives the source second-moment sum with its N/2 factor. Opposite parity of j-i and i+j-1 cancels the constant terms; the remaining cotangent-square difference equals the quotient of positive sine products. Hence every off-diagonal sign and the same-parity pair count hold for every N and every L>0. Q has zero row sum. The N<=2 semigroups are explicitly nonnegative; N>=3 has H13(t)=t Q13+O(t^2)<0. Cauchy–Schwarz controls all nonzero spectral modes for eventual positivity. Exact rational three-node projectors and a strictly increasing cubic prove the small-grid recovery threshold. The embedded independent modal-sum versus closed-form program passed 19,645 finite checks; only the written proof supplies the general quantifiers.

originality.rationale: The assessed novel component is the full, all-grid, explicitly signed off-diagonal generator identity, exact negative-coupling count, and sharp N<=2 unconditional nodal positivity classification for the unfiltered Neumann DCT-II heat method. Kim et al. supplied the method and numerical violations, not this all-dimension sign law in the inspected full text. Periodic Fourier estimates and finite-difference DCT diagonalizations do not directly state this Neumann spectral p^2 operator property. The three-node late-positive time shape is covered in principle by a broader self-adjoint three-spectral-level statement and is treated only as an illustrative specialization, not independent novelty. A classical folded Fourier differentiation matrix may imply the sign identity, which is retained as substantive publication-priority uncertainty.

value.rationale: The 2023 motivating article reports numerical failures of nodal maximum principles for an otherwise exact spatial diffusion step. A complete symbolic sign classification for every off-diagonal coupling at every spatial resolution directly explains why arbitrary-nodal-data positivity fails, identifies the sharp smallest affected grid, and counts precisely all immediate negative influences. The exact three-node recovery and a universal sufficient waiting-time bound show the phenomenon is initially negative yet eventually positive, supplying concrete test cases for positivity-preserving splitting analyses. This is a motivated complete structural classification, not an arbitrary parameter slice or a generic finite check. No general-grid sharp waiting time or nonlinear diffusion conclusion is claimed.
